questions.question: Explain how HIV and AIDS affected South Africa's population, and what changed it.
questions.expected_answer: Before treatment was widely available (late 1990s and early 2000s), AIDS caused hundreds of thousands of deaths a year; death rates rose, life expectancy fell from about 62 (1990) to about 53 (mid-2000s), many children were orphaned and population growth slowed. From 2004 the ARV roll-out (the world's largest) and prevention of mother-to-child transmission lowered deaths, and life expectancy recovered to over 65 by 2019.

questions.question: For TB and malaria, state the cause, how each spreads and two prevention methods.
questions.expected_answer: TB: a bacterium, spread through the air by coughing/sneezing; prevention: ventilation/open windows, covering coughs, early testing and completing treatment, BCG vaccine. Malaria: a Plasmodium parasite spread by the bite of female Anopheles mosquitoes; prevention: insecticide-treated nets, indoor spraying, removing standing water, repellent/long sleeves, anti-malaria tablets for travellers.

questions.question: Why does diarrhoea kill young children, and how can these deaths be prevented?
questions.expected_answer: Diarrhoea causes dehydration (loss of water and salts), which can kill a small child within a day or two. Prevention: safe/treated drinking water, proper sanitation and toilets, handwashing with soap, safe food storage, breastfeeding and the rotavirus vaccine. Treatment: oral rehydration solution (clean water, sugar and salt) and zinc.
